svg.title: Oklahoma region earthquake epicenters in two equal four-year periods, 2013–2016 and 2022–2025, hexbin density plot
svg.desc: 2253 magnitude-3-or-higher USGS earthquakes fall in the Oklahoma-region bounding rectangle in 2013–2016, versus 61 in 2022–2025. Each georeferenced epicenter contributes to one 24 kilometer radius hexagon and identical count color scale. Source dataset 3079 regional records from 2000–October 29 2026. Rectangular study area includes nearby Kansas and Texas, not Oklahoma alone.
svg.text: OKLAHOMA EARTHQUAKES | A SPATIAL BEFORE AND AFTER
M3.0+ epicenters from USGS ComCat · Equal four-year windows · Study area includes nearby border states
Four full years, including the 2015 peak
Four full years, same hexagons and color scale
Only six events in full year 2025
Fewer recorded events in the later four-year window: 97.3% lower
Legend · number of M3+ epicenters per hexagon (same scale in both panels):
Source: USGS ComCat events, 2000–Oct. 29, 2026; Live Atlas frozen extraction (CC BY 4.0). Grid is geographic, not a hazard forecast.
